opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for this role. Maximum allowable is write; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E040 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training max out at read; admin is never permitted for contractors. Recommend granting read.
reason: Jacob Ellison (E040) requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and E040 is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted (admin requires that the employee's role owns the system). Per the HR record, E040 is full-time, so the maximum allowable is write. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: write. (Note: the Security note lists E040 as a contractor with basic training, which would cap at read, but even under the full-time HR record the outcome is that admin is denied and the grant is capped below admin.)
